pr_title: stm32: Add support for G0 series and add BOARD_G0B1RE board dfn.
pr_body:
This commit adds support for the STM32G0 series of MCUs, and a board
definition for BOARD_G0B1RE .  This board has the REPL on UART2 which is
connected to the on-board ST-link USB-UART.
Closes #8292
pr_comments:
Thanks for the contribution, it looks good!

I do not yet have a G0 board.  What sort of testing did you do?  Did you test reading/writing the internal filesystem?

As for the testing, I followed the [Writing Tests](https://docs.micropython.org/en/latest/develop/writingtests.html) instructions, and ran the tests on the board using `python run-tests.py --target minimal --device COM4 >> test_result.txt`.

The results, after filtering passed and skipped tests, are:
```
FAIL  extmod/uselect_poll_basic.py
FAIL  extmod/uselect_poll_udp.py
FAIL  extmod/usocket_udp_nonblock.py
FAIL  extmod/utime_res.py
FAIL  extmod/utime_time_ns.py
FAIL  extmod/vfs_fat_mtime.py
FAIL  micropython/import_mpy_native_gc.py
688 tests performed (19809 individual testcases)
681 tests passed
105 tests skipped: array_construct_endian btree1 btree_error {omitted}
7 tests failed: import_mpy_native_gc uselect_poll_basic uselect_poll_udp usocket_udp_nonblock utime_res utime_time_ns vfs_fat_mtime
```

I just noticed that I had my editor set to use tabs instead of 4 spaces.
I'll run tools/codeformat.py later and push again on a style-only commit.

Regarding reading/writing the internal filesystem, because the STM32G0 is an ARM Cortex M0+, the NVIC register does not have a `NVIC->STIR` register (used by `storage_systick_callback(uint32_t ticks_ms)` in storage.c).

I did some research, and found [this article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/interrupt-controller), where the first few paragraphs indicate that `NVIC->STIR = FLASH_IRQn;` can be replaced with `HAL_NVIC_SetPendingIRQ(FLASH_IRQn);`.

I tried it and I was able to successfully write/read to internal storage (see picture below).
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36895998/156671459-0884ab49-aea4-4443-bf34-81488c7be3cb.png)

I haven't pushed these changes because, as the article explains, the `NVIC->STIR` can be readily modified from the User Space, but `HAL_NVIC_SetPendingIRQ(..)` requires additional changes.

Oh, I forgot to mention, I'm using the STM32 G0 HAL as provided by ST (no modifications), pulled directly through the tool in stm32lib.
It is not as clear to me how/if I should branch and create a Pull Request for that too.
What would be the next step there?
I can confirm that the change to `storage.c` works for f0. Tested on NUCLEO_F091RC. Tested creating LFS1 filesystem, writing and reading main.py. I have a PR in the works.

> I can confirm that the change to `storage.c` works for f0. Tested on NUCLEO_F091RC. Tested creating LFS1 filesystem, writing and reading main.py. I have a PR in the works.

Thanks for the feedback! I'm glad it is working on F0 too.

> > The results, after filtering passed and skipped tests, are:
> 
> OK, that is good, it's fine if only those 7 tests fail.
> 
> > I'll run tools/codeformat.py later and push again on a style-only commit.

> 
> OK, so I suggest a patch like this:
> 
> ```diff
> --- a/ports/stm32/storage.c
> +++ b/ports/stm32/storage.c
> @@ -83,7 +83,11 @@ uint32_t storage_get_block_count(void) {
>  static void storage_systick_callback(uint32_t ticks_ms) {
>      if (STORAGE_IDLE_TICK(ticks_ms)) {
>          // Trigger a FLASH IRQ to execute at a lower priority
> +        #if __CORTEX_M == 0
> +        NVIC_SetPendingIRQ(FLASH_IRQn);
> +        #else
>          NVIC->STIR = FLASH_IRQn;
> +        #endif
>      }
>  }
> ```
> 
> That should hopefully get storage working on Cortex-M0 MCUs.
> 
> > Oh, I forgot to mention, I'm using the STM32 G0 HAL as provided by ST (no modifications), pulled directly through the tool in stm32lib.
> > It is not as clear to me how/if I should branch and create a Pull Request for that too.
> > What would be the next step there?
> 
> It's easiest for me to just add the G0 HAL to stm32lib, and update everything. I can do that just before this PR gets merged.

Is there anything else I should do?

Hello AsenioL and thanks for supporting STM32G0.
I've tried to compile with:
```
make V=1 BOARD=NUCLEO_G0B1RE
make: ***  No rule to make target "build-NUCLEO_G0B1RE/modstm_qstr.h", needed by "build-NUCLEO_G0B1RE/genhdr/qstrdefs.generated.h".  Stop.
 
```
Looking on the forum I see that the problem is maybe related to "hal and cmsis files has not update", but I've no mean to fix that. Can you kindly help with that? Thank you

It is likely that the problem you're running into is that you're missing those files (CMSIS and HAL) since they have not yet been included in the **stm32lib** submodule.

In that case, what you need to do is:
1. Clone the CMSIS + HAL from the STM32G0 github ([link](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0)) to _lib/stm32lib_ inside your local copy of the project. This should create a new folder with a name like `STM32CubeG0`
2. Go to _lib/stm32lib_ on your terminal and run `fetch_from_upstream.sh STM32G0 STM32CubeG0`.

The script should create all the files you are missing. Try recompiling and see if it works.

Code has been rebased and is ready to be reviewed.
Commit messages have also been fixed.
There are no conflicts now!

Thanks very much for the hard work on this PR!  The commits are nice and clean.  I tested building PYBV10, PYBD_SF6 and NUCLEO_WB55 and they produce identical firmware before and after this PR, which is very good, it means that the commits here do not touch other MCUs.

I updated stm32lib to include G0 at v1.5.1.  This builds against the NUCLEO_G0B1RE board but I did not test it.

issue_context.title: Adding support for STM32G0 MCUs
issue_context.body:
Hi I have been working on adding support for STM32G0 MCUs. Particularly, the ST NUCLEO_G0B1RE for a couple of weeks, and today I got it to compile, link and run finally. I was also able run the run-tests.py script (see results below).
This is my first contribution to a project.

This requires the stm32lib repository to be updated to include HAL and CMSIS for the STM32G0.
comments:
What is the best way to share my changes?
Should I fork and push them there?
The contributing guidelines and the git history show small and concise changes on each commit, and this would require several changes to around 20 files

See this commit for when STM32G4 support was added: 8f68e26f79ee325669fb7dc7bbd092fccd5b038f

In general each commit should be self contained, and adding a new MCU series is (usually) one logical operation, so should be one commit.  You also want a separate commit (but can be in the same PR) to add the board definition files for the new board, in this case `NUCLEO_G0B1RE`.  It's also nice if you can find an image of the board for the micropython-media repo (so the board can be built automatically for micropython.org/download).

Best way to make progress here is to push your changes to a branch of your fork of this repo, then open a PR here for that branch.  Then we can discuss further.
Thanks, I'll start working on that.

I just created branch: https://github.com/AsensioL/micropython/tree/support_stm32g0
I pulled from master, and resolving conflicts right now. I also noticed MCU families tend to be grouped alphabetically, so I'm making that way too.

While porting the code for the G0, on powerctrl.c...
- I used the SR register for the wake up flags (WUTF...), which looked similar to the STM32H7A3xx and STM32H7B3xx port ([link](https://github.com/AsensioL/micropython/commit/f674d53c84cb2d3b9e67958c2dacd6a8fbb74ea3#r66615271))
- But I noticed that, on the G4/WL port, the MISR register is used. Is that right?

Since I'm not sure, I'm going to merge the code for the G0 like the G4/WL, but I thougth I should mention.

Edit: Similar thing in stm32_it.c 
- I used the RTC->SR->WUTF register for the G0 port, like STM32H7A3xx and STM32H7B3 ([link](https://github.com/AsensioL/micropython/commit/f674d53c84cb2d3b9e67958c2dacd6a8fbb74ea3#r66628551))
- The G4 port relies on WL port relies on RTC->MISR->WUTMF
Again, since I'm not sure, I merged to code of the G0 to match the one of the G4/WL

Pulled from master and conflicts resolved.
Waiting for feedback now.
https://github.com/AsensioL/micropython/tree/support_stm32g0
Please open a pull request from that branch to this repo.
